minor_characters.name: Earl of Berkeley (Hereditary Diaperer)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Appears at Tom’s first royal dinner to tie on a napkin and perform comic, ceremonial service.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He contributes only etiquette-comedy and pageantry; removing him does not affect plot, themes, or any main character’s arc.

minor_characters.name: Lord d’Arcy (First Groom of the Chamber)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Listed among the dinner-service functionaries supervising Tom’s first meal.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A one-note ceremonial presence whose removal trims court-comedy without touching story stakes.

minor_characters.name: Norroy King-at-Arms
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One of the many titled attendants in Tom’s dressing-and-hose-passing scene.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Purely decorative to the court pageant; cutting him doesn’t change Tom’s learning curve or the Great Seal thread.

minor_characters.name: Master of the Wardrobe
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Another link in the comic ‘pass the garment’ chain during Tom’s dressing ritual.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Eliding him streamlines ceremony lists without cost to character or plot.

minor_characters.name: Chief Equerry in Waiting
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Presides over the farcical hose mishap in the Chapter 14 dressing procession.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His role is an etiquette gag; excising it leaves Tom’s court-bewilderment intact elsewhere.

minor_characters.name: Lord High Admiral (in Tom’s dinner/dressing sequences)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Figures in the comically overstaffed household scenes, distinct from the statesman Somerset.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He adds pageant texture only; the political Lord Protector storyline remains unaffected.

minor_characters.name: Garter King-at-Arms
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named among heraldic dignitaries in procession lists.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A heraldic flourish whose absence won’t change any action or thematic beat.

minor_characters.name: Lady Mary (Mary Tudor) cameo
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Tom gently rebukes his ‘sister’ for severity in a brief audience-scene.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her cameo isn’t required for Tom’s mercy arc (amply shown elsewhere) or for the Great Seal climax.

minor_characters.name: Lord Guilford Dudley
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Briefly named when denied admittance during a court visit.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A one-line historical nod that doesn’t affect character motivations or events.

minor_characters.name: Dot-and-go-One; The Bat; Black Bess; The Wen
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named vagabonds in the tramps’ barn chapter and campfire scenes.
minor_characters.reason_removable: They supply colour but no turning points; Miles, John Canty, and the Ruffler suffice to carry Edward’s beggar-world ordeal.

minor_characters.name: Sir William Herbert
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A courtier who escorts Tom within the palace and manages servants in a brief scene.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Interchangeable with unnamed attendants; trimming him leaves Tom’s court initiation and isolation unchanged.

minor_characters.name: Sir Humphrey Marlow (old court officer)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Miles tries to send in his name to this old household official before being detained at the palace.
minor_characters.reason_removable: This named target for Miles’s failed errand can be omitted without affecting his entry to the recognition scene.

subplots.name: Humphrey Marlow, the whipping-boy, and his ‘Hereditary Grand Whipping-Boy’ elevation
subplots.reason_removable: Though funny and topical, it is not required for Tom’s mercy arc or the Great Seal resolution, and compressing court lessons elsewhere preserves the same beats.

subplots.name: ‘Foo-foo the First’: Edward’s mock crowning by vagabonds
subplots.reason_removable: This extended humiliation repeats the theme already achieved by Edward’s capture, forced begging, and the stocks scene, and cutting it leaves his beggar-world education and resolve intact.

subplots.name: Miles’s errand to find Sir Humphrey Marlow before his palace arrest
subplots.reason_removable: The detour adds a near-miss complication but doesn’t change Miles’s ultimate audience or the recognition climax; he can be brought straight to the throne room.

subplots.name: Civic masques and set-pieces of Tom’s recognition procession (excluding the mother’s appearance)
subplots.chapter_span: Ch 11 and Ch 31 (pageants, mummeries, and guild tableaux)
subplots.reason_removable: The ornate tableaux and mummery lists can be condensed to keep Tom’s awe and the pivotal shock of his mother’s kiss without the side-shows.

subplots.name: London Bridge free-for-all and falling-severed-head episode
subplots.reason_removable: A colourful riot that neither advances the coronation interruption nor develops a principal character.

digressions.topic: Long architectural and urban description of London and Offal Court before Tom’s home life begins
digressions.reason_removable: These touristic paragraphs can be pruned while keeping Tom’s poverty, family, and Father Andrew’s influence.

digressions.topic: Inventory of household offices and comic etiquette at Tom’s first dinner (napkin, taster, etc.)
digressions.reason_removable: A lengthy ceremonial catalogue that adds humour but not new stakes or insight beyond Tom’s already clear court-bewilderment.

digressions.topic: The river pageant’s barge-by-barge descriptions and decorative inventory
digressions.reason_removable: Lavish spectacle that can be summarized without loss to plot or theme.

digressions.topic: Guildhall apparel lists, mommarye, and costume catalogues during the civic feast
digressions.reason_removable: Pageant texture only; trimming these keeps the key beats (Tom’s reception and the ‘King is dead’ reversal).

digressions.topic: Essayistic aside on London Bridge as a self-contained town (shops, history, heads on spikes)
digressions.reason_removable: An excellent vignette but halts the story; Edward and Miles’s progress reads cleanly without it.

digressions.topic: The hyper-detailed dressing rite and the ‘missing truss-point tag’ hose fiasco
digressions.reason_removable: An extended etiquette gag that can be condensed to a line without affecting Tom’s position or the Great Seal tension.

digressions.topic: ‘The State Dinner’: gold plate inventories, Benvenuto work, and etiquette gags (rosewater, nose-itching)
digressions.reason_removable: Sustained comic business that duplicates Tom’s court-naïveté already established elsewhere.

digressions.topic: Canting song lyrics and roster of tramps (knife-grinder, barber-surgeon, etc.)
digressions.reason_removable: Colourful taxonomy that can be cut while keeping Edward’s peril among vagabonds and the stocks episode.

digressions.topic: Recognition procession’s exhaustive participant lists and heraldic flourishes
digressions.reason_removable: The procession can be summarized to reach the essential turn: Tom’s mother breaking through and his shamed denial.

digressions.topic: Peeresses’ diamond ‘Milky Way,’ sunrise optics, and multi-page seating/lighting tableau in the Abbey
digressions.reason_removable: A beautiful pause that stalls momentum before the Great Seal test; the coronation crisis reads more tautly without it.
